prompt:
Create an original six-pose right-facing action sprite sheet for Paprika's JAMVERSE '96 `pass-behind` basketball animation. Use the attached Paprika pass and shot sheets as the exact character identity and sprite-style references. Paprika is canonically a REAL TINY FOUR-FOOTED KIT FOX: horizontal fox body, russet-orange fur, cream-white muzzle/chest/underside, huge triangular ears, bright fox eyes, pointed muzzle, a large bushy tail with a pale tip, and her fitted purple-and-gold sports vest. Preserve her established natural small-fox proportions and all four animal legs. She must remain quadruped in every pose: never anthropomorphic, human-shaped, upright like a person, or equipped with hands, shoes, shorts, or a cloak.

Draw exactly 6 distinct, complete, independently redrawn full-body fox poses on a true transparent RGBA background, arranged in 3 columns by 2 rows in strict left-to-right, top-to-bottom order. Keep the same figure scale and a stable paw baseline. Leave generous empty transparent space around every figure and between every cell so the tall ears, muzzle, paws, and entire pale tail tip stay inside the cell; no clipping, touching, overlap, fused figures, cell outlines, grid lines, or panels. Match the crisp, colorful, richly shaded 1990s arcade pixel-sprite style and palette of the references. No basketball is drawn: gameplay renders and tracks the separate ball at Paprika's muzzle. No floor, shadow, court, hoop, opponent, extra person, prop, lettering, numerals, logos, glow, or background.

Pose sequence for a fox pass-behind using a natural backward muzzle-flick, never human arms: (0) gather low on all four paws, muzzle near the invisible ball, looking forward; (1) crouch lower and shift her weight onto braced hind paws, tail extended for balance; (2) coil her shoulders and turn her head back over her shoulder to check the teammate behind, forepaws planted; (3) RELEASE anchor: snap the pointed muzzle backward behind her body toward the teammate, keep all paws animal-like and the mouth empty, no ball or other object; (4) follow through with a compact body twist, tail sweeping opposite the throw and one forepaw naturally lightening from the floor; (5) recover on all four paws and bring her head forward. Keep the fox body facing mostly right while the head and shoulders visibly rotate for the behind-the-body pass. Every pose is different and anatomically plausible for the same small fox; do not repeat, warp, or duplicate any pose.

review.notes: Visual/source review confirms six distinct full-body right-facing kit-fox poses in 3x2 row-major cells, RGBA transparency, no ball or props, quadruped anatomy throughout, in-bounds ears/paws/tail, and a visible frame-3 backward muzzle-flick with the fox body still facing right. All six alpha>=64 body components are separate; none is clipped or excluded.
